children.text: A Mechanical Model for Phase Transitions

A bead of mass m slides on a ring of radius R rotating about its vertical diameter at angular speed \(\omega\). Angle \(\theta\) is measured from the downward vertical, with \(-\pi/2<\theta<\pi/2\). Let \(\omega_c=\sqrt{g/R}\). In the stated rotating-frame model, the only forces are gravity, the radial normal N, centrifugal force and opposing tangential force \(-fkN\), with \(f=\operatorname{sgn}\dot\theta\). Use this simplified force diagram, omitting any additional forces. For B.1 through B.9 set k=0. Landau free energy has the form \(V(\mathcal M)=a(T)\mathcal M^2+b(T)\mathcal M^4\), with b positive and a changing sign at the transition. Expansions \(\sin\theta=\theta-\theta^3/6+\cdots\), \(\cos\theta=1-\theta^2/2+\theta^4/24+\cdots\) may be used.

statement.text:
A Mechanical Model for Phase Transitions
A bead of mass m slides on a ring of radius R rotating about its vertical diameter at angular speed \(\omega\). Angle \(\theta\) is measured from the downward vertical, with \(-\pi/2<\theta<\pi/2\). Let \(\omega_c=\sqrt{g/R}\). In the stated rotating-frame model, the only forces are gravity, the radial normal N, centrifugal force and opposing tangential force \(-fkN\), with \(f=\operatorname{sgn}\dot\theta\). Use this simplified force diagram, omitting any additional forces. For B.1 through B.9 set k=0. Landau free energy has the form \(V(\mathcal M)=a(T)\mathcal M^2+b(T)\mathcal M^4\), with b positive and a changing sign at the transition. Expansions \(\sin\theta=\theta-\theta^3/6+\cdots\), \(\cos\theta=1-\theta^2/2+\theta^4/24+\cdots\) may be used.


A.1. Radial and tangential equations
Write both equations of motion, with angle increasing counterclockwise.
B.1. Equilibrium branches
Find equilibrium angles in terms of \(\omega,\omega_c\).
B.2. Equilibrium-angle plot
Sketch equilibrium angles against \(\omega/\omega_c\).
B.3. Normal-reaction plot
Sketch normal-reaction magnitude at stable equilibrium against the rotation-rate ratio.
B.4. Effective-potential coefficients
With \(F_\theta=-R^{-1}dV/d\theta\), \(V(0)=0\), and \(V=P+Q\cos\theta+S\sin^2\theta\), determine P,Q,S.
B.5. Quartic expansion
Find \(a(\omega),b(\omega)\) in \(V\simeq a\theta^2+b\theta^4\).
B.6. Potential plots
Sketch V against angle for \(\omega/\omega_c=0.9\) and 5, without detailed plotting calculations.
B.7. Critical-exponent analogy
For magnetization \(\mathcal M=\mathcal M_0(1-T/T_c)^{1/2}\) below \(T_c\), identify mechanical analogues and the bead critical exponent.
B.8. Small-oscillation frequency
Find \(\Omega_0=R^{-1}\sqrt{V^{\prime\prime}(\theta_0)/m}\) about stable equilibria.
B.9. Frequency plot
Sketch the small-oscillation frequency against rotation rate.
C.1. Opposing-force equilibrium
Now take \(f=1,k=\tan\alpha\). Write the limiting equilibrium condition as \((\omega/\omega_c)^2=\tan x/\sin y\), and identify x,y.
C.2. Representative frictional angles
For \(f=1,k=0.05\), estimate the equilibrium angles for \(\omega/\omega_c=0.50\) and 0.70.

children.text: A Mechanical Model for Phase Transitions

With N directed towards the centre, \[mR\dot\theta^2=N-mg\cos\theta-mR\omega^2\sin^2\theta,\] \[mR\ddot\theta=mR\omega^2\sin\theta\cos\theta-mg\sin\theta-fkN.\] These are the stipulated two-component model.

The tangential equation gives \(\sin\theta_0(\omega^2\cos\theta_0-\omega_c^2)=0\). The branch \(\theta_0=0\) always exists. For \(\omega>\omega_c\), additional branches are \(\theta_0=\pm\arccos(\omega_c^2/\omega^2)\). The zero branch becomes unstable above threshold.
The stable zero branch continues to ratio 1, where it bifurcates continuously into two symmetric stable branches approaching \(\pm\pi/2\). Show the remaining zero branch as unstable above 1.

Below threshold the bead sits at the bottom and \(N=mg\). Above threshold substitute \(\cos\theta_0=\omega_c^2/\omega^2\) in the radial equation to get \(N=mR\omega^2\). The curve is continuous at the threshold and then quadratic.
Integrating the tangential force gives \[V=mgR(1-\cos\theta)-\tfrac12mR^2\omega^2\sin^2\theta.\] Thus \(P=mgR,Q=-mgR,S=-mR^2\omega^2/2\).

Expand both cosine and sine squared through fourth order: \[a=\frac{mgR}{2}(1-\omega^2/\omega_c^2),\qquad b=\frac{mgR}{6}(\omega^2/\omega_c^2-1/4).\] In particular the quartic coefficient is positive near the transition.

At 0.9, V has one minimum at zero. At 5, the zero-angle point is a local maximum between symmetric minima at \(\pm\arccos(1/25)\). Use the full potential on the allowed interval for the distant minima, since a small-angle quartic expansion is not accurate there.

Near threshold, \(1-\theta_0^2/2\simeq\omega_c^2/\omega^2\), so \(\theta_0\simeq\pm\sqrt2(1-\omega_c^2/\omega^2)^{1/2}\). Thus magnetization corresponds to \(\theta_0\), reduced temperature to \(\omega_c^2/\omega^2\), and the exponent is \(\beta=1/2\). Equivalently use \(\sin\theta_0\) and reduced temperature \(\omega_c^4/\omega^4\).

At zero below threshold, \(\Omega_0=\sqrt{\omega_c^2-\omega^2}\). At the nonzero stable branches above threshold, \(\Omega_0=\omega\sqrt{1-\omega_c^4/\omega^4}\). Both tend to zero at threshold, where a harmonic approximation has zero stiffness.

The curve starts at \(\Omega_0=\omega_c\) for zero rotation, decreases to zero at \(\omega_c\), then rises and approaches \(\Omega_0\sim\omega\). Both sides have the square-root softening near threshold.

With zero velocity and acceleration in the stipulated limiting-force model, \[\frac{\omega^2}{\omega_c^2}=\frac{\sin\theta_0+k\cos\theta_0}{\sin\theta_0(\cos\theta_0-k\sin\theta_0)}=\frac{\tan(\theta_0+\alpha)}{\sin\theta_0}.\] Thus \(x=\theta_0+\alpha,y=\theta_0\). The equality prescribes a directional limiting friction force. True static friction would allow an interval bounded by this force rather than a unique equilibrium equality.

Using \(\tan(\theta_0+\alpha)\simeq\theta_0+k\) and \(\sin\theta_0\simeq\theta_0\), \[\theta_0\simeq k/[(\omega/\omega_c)^2-1].\] The estimates are \(-0.0667\) and \(-0.0980\) radians, rounded to \(-0.07,-0.10\) in the source. Exact roots of the limiting-force equation are approximately \(-0.0665,-0.0971\) radians.
